NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday demanded the immediate suspension of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and called for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation or prosecution. Their demand comes after the Election Commission issued a fresh statement defending its decisions amid reported differences within the poll body.Congress leaders Pawan Khera and Jairam Ramesh accused the EC of going into "damage control" mode following an Indian Express report and subsequent media coverage on differences between the three election commissioners. The party alleged that the SIR exercise had led to the "disenfranchisement" of crores of voters and questioned the Commission's explanation on changes to Form 6, used to add names to electoral rolls."The ECI's press note today is too lame, too little, too late," Congress' head of media and publicity department Pawan Khera said.Ramesh said the Commission had issued the statement only after the media reports and nationwide protests seeking Kumar's removal."It has just issued a wishy-washy Press Note that raises further questions on its intent, integrity, impartiality and credibility," he said on X."The ongoing SIR, which has turned out to be a method of massive disenfranchisement of several crores of Indians, must be suspended immediately without delay."In the meantime, nothing short of the CEC's resignation or prosecution will suffice," he said in a two-page statement.The Election Commission said all SIR orders were issued after approval from all three Election Commissioners. It also said changes to Form 6 had been upheld by the Supreme Court.The Commission further said letters written by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary were not related to any policy decision of the Commission or its IT division. According to the EC, the letters concerned the functioning of an officer deputed to the poll body.Ramesh said the EC statement did not directly deny the findings reported by the Indian Express."First, the Press note does not directly deny the story or its findings. It makes a defensive attempt to downplay the same in paragraph 3(i) and 3(ii) but does not say that the allegations are baseless," he said.On Goa, he said the EC's response showed that 81 of the 97 deleted voters had already filled Form 6 to be included again in the electoral rolls."To put this another way, you disenfranchise voters through a broken and corrupt system, and when caught say that they are being added back," Ramesh said.Khera also alleged that the EC had not addressed objections raised by the other two Election Commissioners over changes to Form 6."That objection was not resolved then. It was not resolved since. And this 'mother of all objections' has still not been addressed - even after today's so-called unanimous meeting," Khera said on X."So until the ECI answers this specific legal objection, no length of press notes, no claim of unanimity or any other clownery can save Gyanesh Kumar Gupta's face," he said."It is still not too late for him. He should resign and turn approver, or prepare for jail," Khera added.Ramesh also questioned the EC's reliance on a Supreme Court order of May 27 saying the order had preceded the recent media revelations."The order which was pronounced well before the recent revelations will not save the CEC for the malicious deletion of targeted voters, for the incompetence that has resulted in citizens being wiped off the roles, for the crores lost in both expenses and man-hours due to the confusion and harassment caused to entire families," he said.He also questioned the extension of voter registration deadlines in Delhi and Maharashtra and asked what would happen to voters in Karnataka, Telangana, Bihar and West Bengal."What happens to the voters disenfranchised in Bihar and West Bengal? Do the voters of these and other states who were deleted due to one man's corruption not deserve answers," Ramesh said.The Congress leader also criticised the EC's decision to involve experts from IITs and IIITs to review the ECINET portal and submit a report on whether it complies with rules."Aside from being a meaningless safeguard (since the concern is not about the technical soundness but rather the centralization which prevents voter addition at ground level) this confirms the concerns attributed to the two other Election Commissioners per the reportage," he said.Ramesh alleged that the EC's statement had not addressed concerns over the deletion of young voters."The Press Note avoids answering the questions regarding the deliberate targeting of Gen Z voters. The ECI has no answer for its targeted disenfranchisement, beginning mid-July through wholly illegal changes made to Form 6 (unseen and unapproved by Parliament) which placed an unfair burden on them to find and disclose their parents and/or grandparents' details," he said.He listed several allegations that he said required answers, including the "unilateral nature of decision making by the CEC", alleged bias against the Opposition, alleged participation in "vote chori", the enrolment of Gen Z voters and alleged negligence in the deletion and updating of electoral rolls.Ramesh said the CEC could not avoid scrutiny through bureaucratic procedures."He stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable," Ramesh said.
Article Summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said the Commission had issued the statement only after the media reports and nationwide protests seeking Kumar's removal. The party alleged that the SIR exercise had led to the "disenfranchisement" of crores of voters and questioned the Commission's explanation on changes to Form 6.

NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann will hold a meeting of the seven-member coordination committee constituted to examine the amended anti-sacrilege law, at his residence here on Sunday.At the meeting to be held at 1 pm, the committee will deliberate on provisions of the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 and matters related to its implementation, with an aim to uphold the highest standards of 'satkar' (reverence) for the Sikh Holy Book Guru Granth Sahib, according to an official statement issued on Saturday.All members of the coordination committee will attend the meeting.The seven-member panel comprises former Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Raghbir Singh, Sant Giani Harnaam Singh Khalsa, Sant Baba Sewa Singh, former Justices Jaswinder Singh and Gurbir Singh, former IPS officer Jatinder Singh Aulakh and Advocate Preet Inder Paul Singh.The amendment bill was unanimously passed by the Punjab Assembly on April 13. Article Title: Air India crash probe: Pilots' body seeks formal consideration of its tech submissions

NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has urged the civil aviation ministry to ensure that its technical submissions on the Air India AI171 crash are formally considered before the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) finalises its probe report.The AAIB investigation into the June 12, 2025 crash in Ahmedabad, which killed 260 people, is at an advanced stage.In a letter to civil aviation minister K Rammohan Naidu on Friday, FIP sought to be nominated as an “independent technical participant in the review of the draft AI171 final investigation report”.FIP said it had “reliably learnt that the government/ ministry has directed or is considering requiring the draft report to undergo examination by an independent committee before it is circulated/ finalised”. It said that if such a review mechanism is being constituted, the pilots' body should be formally nominated and represented as an independent technical stakeholder representing the professional pilot community.The federation also requested that its technical submissions receive formal and documented consideration before the final report is issued.The FIP had last week urged the AAIB to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of electrical-system evidence related to Boeing 787 aircraft as part of the AI171 investigation.The Air India Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner, registered as VT-ANB, crashed shortly after taking off from Ahmedabad for London Gatwick on June 12, 2025. Of the 242 people on board, 241 died, while 19 people on the ground were also killed. All 12 crew members died and one passenger survived.The aircraft, manufactured in 2013 and powered by GE engines, had flown 41,868 hours. Its Airworthiness Review Certificate was valid until May 23, 2026.In its latest update on the investigation, the AAIB said significant progress had been made and that the final report would be released after completion of all investigative activities and the required international review and consultation processes.The bureau has said the investigation team has examined technical, operational, organisational and human factors associated with the accident, without disclosing specific findings from the probe.
Article Summary: The AAIB investigation into the June 12, 2025 crash in Ahmedabad, which killed 260 people, is at an advanced stage. FIP sought to be nominated as an “independent technical participant in the review of the draft AI171 final investigation report’
